analysis.title: GS McGeoch - GS Materials Nov 16: Iron ore drawdown ... Stay short (for now)
key_insights: Iron ore fell to 4-year lows overnight, below $88/t. Onshore traders are bearish across the board. Trade houses were liquidating below $90, producers were hedging, and consumer flow was elevated on the other side.

Hot steel production fell 3ktpd w/w against a consensus of -10k. It is still expected to weaken in the forward period, so McGeoch frames the move as a point-in-time call rather than a price-level call.
McGeoch stays short iron ore 'for choice'. There is no CMRG solution in sight for FMG, and the RIO and VALE updates are about 3 weeks away.

He does not expect Australian government intervention soon. He cites the pace of government action and notes the government is only now looking at the issue. The government has commented on value destruction, quoting $10bn, which matches a GS report from the prior week on CMRG and $10bn of value leakage.

Miners keep adding supply (Simandou, Liberia at peak in Q4) while the China steel outlook is weak. McGeoch has heard discussion of China domestic steel demand falling 60-80mt in 2027, though he has not seen it formalized.
GS is cutting its 2027 iron ore forecast to $90/t.

VALE capital markets day is in early Dec (1 Dec) and RIO will give a short update with 2027 production guidance. VALE produces 335-345mt in 2026, with medium term 340-360mt and long term 360mt+. RIO 2026 guidance is 323-338mt with a target of 345-360mt.

The VALE CEO at the GS conference said 10% or 160mt of supply is at risk at spot prices, of which 15mt has been cut. He is more bullish than spot, citing China steel resilience, Vietnam (25 to 100mt) and India (175 to 600mt), and value over volume. He sees only 5mt at risk for VALE.
McGeoch argues for supply discipline: 300mt at $100 is more profitable than 330mt at $75. He suggests that if China acts as one buyer, Australia should act as one seller.

GS reduced its bullish bias on EU natural gas because prices rallied despite higher LNG flows. Middle East exports are at about 40% of pre-conflict levels and tracking toward 50%. European weather has been colder than seasonal but is forecast to move closer to normal over the next two weeks. The JKM/TTF spread has weakened, which indicates a diminished Asian physical bid.

Speculative clients are net long EU gas, especially on VaR metrics. The upside tail from cold weather or reduced flows keeps prices above GS's modal outcome. This makes short positions hard to hold without a view on mild weather or Middle East flows.

A resumption of Russian gas flows is a tail risk (<20% probability) as US talks intensify. Prices would fall quickly if the market priced it in. EUR7 intraday moves, including Friday's with no headline, make holding delta difficult. GS prefers optionalising delta, with length in call spreads at the very front of the curve.

GS weekly commodity thoughts: oil vol is now in contango as flows reposition down the curve, and aluminium shows record backwardation in prompt spreads. GS is taking profit on its bullish US gas spreads recommendation.

China wrap: risk-off across the region with tech hardware names under heavy selling. STAR 50 fell as much as 6.18% and ChiNext as much as 4.83% intraday before recouping some. SHCOMP closed marginally above 3,600. GS China Banks rose 1.95%, with multiple names at multi-year highs. Retail sales, FAI and IP all missed estimates.
A volume spike in CSI 300 ETFs after about 7 quiet sessions suggests the national team may try to defend SHCOMP 3,600.
Event risk this week: the Trump/Xi/Putin meeting on Thursday (4:45am EUR time) and NVDA earnings.

tension_points.bull_case: The VALE CEO sees China steel as resilient, with Vietnam (25 to 100mt) and India (175 to 600mt) as growth sources. He says 10% or 160mt of supply is at risk at spot prices and favors value over volume. Australian government attention to value leakage could also help, and a smaller drop in hot steel production than expected is a small positive.
tension_points.bear_case: Miners keep adding supply (Simandou, Liberia), China steel demand may fall 60-80mt in 2027, hot metal production is expected to weaken, and no CMRG solution is in sight for FMG.
tension_points.what_invalidates: VALE capital markets day (1 Dec) and the RIO 2027 production guidance update, about 3 weeks away, could bring supply discipline. Australian government intervention would also change the view.

tension_points.bull_case: Cold weather or a reduction in flows would lift prices. Speculative clients are net long on VaR metrics, and the upside tail keeps price above GS's modal outcome.
tension_points.bear_case: Middle East exports are recovering toward 50% of pre-conflict levels, weather is forecast to normalize, and the JKM/TTF spread shows a weaker Asian physical bid. A resumption of Russian flows (<20% probability) would drop prices quickly even if only priced in.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Colder-than-normal weather or lower Middle East export flows would invalidate the reduced bullish bias. Mild weather or a Russian flow headline would invalidate the long.
